issues.legal_issue: A criminal FIR cannot be quashed at the threshold under the inherent jurisdiction when the investigation remains incomplete and material factual matters require investigation.
material_facts: A father lodged an FIR alleging that his son’s wife and her family members had harassed his son and abetted his suicide.
The police investigation was pending, and the record indicated that further inquiry remained to be done.
The suicide notes had been reported to match the deceased’s handwriting, and the FIR raised factual matters including whether the deceased had a prior mental condition.
The High Court assessed the parties’ factual assertions and quashed the FIR before the investigation was completed.
issues.conclusion: The High Court quashed the FIR prematurely. Its order was set aside, and the investigative authorities were directed to complete the investigation promptly and take it to its logical conclusion, without treating the Supreme Court’s observations as findings on the merits.
issues.legal_principle: The inherent power under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure must be exercised cautiously. Consistent with the Court’s prior decisions, an FIR may be quashed when continuing the investigation would amount to an abuse of process; where unresolved factual assertions require investigation, the court should not prematurely determine them while quashing the FIR. The judgment refers to a catena of this Court’s decisions but does not identify them by name. It makes no determination on whether the ingredients of abetment of suicide are ultimately established.

predicates.criminal_fir_quashing_proceeding: A person sought to have a criminal FIR quashed by a court.
predicates.investigation_pending: The investigation into the FIR had not been completed.
predicates.material_factual_questions_require_inves: Material factual matters raised by the allegations remained unresolved and required investigation.

issues.definition: When a person seeks to quash a criminal FIR while its investigation is pending and material factual questions require investigation, the quashing order is set aside and the investigation is to be completed.
